newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - June 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - June 3.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- In one of the first major amendments to the charter draft, the Constitution Drafting Assembly's (CDA) vetting committee has decided to scrap a provision on the direct election of the Senate, citing concerns over political influence in the upper chamber. The draft initially stated that the Senate would consist of directly-elected members and specially-selected senators with the combined membership not exceeding 200. (THE NATION)

- The National Housing Authority governor will be transferred to an inactive post pending a review of an investigation into irregularities in a land scandal in Pathum Thani province. The authority board agrees to propose the transfer of Pree Buranasiri to the Interior Ministry after mistakes are found in the investigation. (BANGKOK POST)

- The Office of the Narcotics Control Board (ONCB) has announced that the government is losing the fight against amphetamine abuse, saying 12 to 18 million tablets of the drug have been smuggled into Thailand in the past six months. An ONCB report submitted to Deputy Prime Minister Sukhavich Rangsitphol says that regular crackdowns on amphetamine production have forced manufacturers to relocate their operations to Burma, Laos and Cambodia. (THE NATION)

- The Petroleum Authority of Thailand does not have permission to build the Yadana gas pipeline through forest areas in Kanchanaburi province, the agriculture minister says. The ministry would have to consider if the project would have adverse effects on forest. The development comes amid a warning by the industry minister that Burma will impose a daily fine of 40 million baht if the pipeline is not completed by July next year. (BANGKOK POST)

- The race to introduce a new export policy takes another leap forward when the Chart Pattana Party, the second largest coalition partner, presents the prime minister with what it describes as the most comprehensive promotion package. The package, worked by former finance minister and adviser to the premier, Surakiart Sathirathai, follows current finance minister and commerce minister's so called "export summit" in Pattaya, with 31 leading exporters, just over a week ago. (THE NATION)
